editorial:
Three sixth-grade best friends find themselves in way over their heads when a broken drone threatens to ruin everything before Max's dad gets home. Max, Thor, and Lucas are the kind of kids who still think kissing is gross but are desperate to look cool at the upcoming party. Their mission to fix the drone spirals into a wild afternoon involving stolen drugs, a sex doll, and a lot of very confused adults. The humor comes from watching these sweet, innocent kids stumble through situations they barely understand, and it lands perfectly because the boys are genuinely likable. You will laugh out loud at their clueless reactions and the way they misinterpret everything around them.

The three young leads carry the whole film with natural, funny performances that never feel forced. The pacing never drags, and the jokes keep coming without wearing out their welcome. Some of the humor is crude, so it is not for everyone, but underneath the raunchy jokes there is a surprisingly sweet story about friendship and growing up. If you enjoy comedies like Superbad but want something a little lighter, this is a great pick. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for your collection.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the boys finally get the drone fixed and make it to the party. Max kisses his crush, Thor decides to quit the school play to focus on what he loves, and Lucas accepts that his parents are getting divorced. The big twist is that the boys realize growing up means their friendship will change, and they might not always be as close. They share an emotional goodbye hug, promising to stay friends even as life pulls them in different directions. It is a surprisingly touching ending that balances the crude humor with real heart.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves coming-of-age comedies with heart
